title: Graph ML Fundamentals
interviewAnswer: A graph represents entities as nodes and relationships as edges. ML on graphs combines node/edge features with graph structure to predict node labels, links, graph properties or rankings.
why: Graph ML starts with representing entities and relationships explicitly; interviews expect you to know nodes, edges, direction, heterogeneity and graph-specific leakage.
intuition: A graph stores objects as nodes and relationships as edges. Features live on nodes/edges, while topology itself provides information that ordinary tabular models may miss.
deepDive: Graphs may be directed/undirected, weighted, homogeneous or heterogeneous with multiple node/edge types. Degree, neighborhoods, paths and connected components describe structure. Adjacency matrices/lists encode connectivity. In ML, splits require care: edges/nodes from the future can leak information, and message passing can indirectly expose validation/test structure depending on the setup.
math: Adjacency A_ij=1 (or weight) when an edge connects i→j. Degree d_i=Σ_j A_ij for a simple directed-out degree.
workedExample: A developer–PR graph has two node types and “authored”/“reviewed” edges. The same PR text alone misses historical reviewer relationships that graph structure captures.
commonMistakes: Treating graph rows as independent samples.
Randomly splitting temporal interaction graphs without leakage analysis.
followUps: How do you split graph data?
production: Graph freshness, edge timestamps and entity resolution matter as much as the GNN. Build reproducible snapshot logic for training and online updates.
